name: Little HERMES
summary: A torso and two legs at roughly a third human scale, built by Joao Ramos and Sangbae Kim to carry the HERMES balance-feedback idea into dynamic locomotion. An operator in a feedback vest ran and jumped in place, and the robot did the same in real time — synchronised to the human, untethered from supports, and staying upright while being struck repeatedly with a hammer and while walking over uneven ground. The work appeared in Science Robotics in October 2019.
notable: Human-synchronised running and jumping via a balance-feedback vest, without tethers or supports
Stayed balanced under repeated hammer blows from varying directions
